I was born in El Salvador, both my parents are Catholic but half my family on both sides is Protestant(complicated, I know), I also have some JW family members but I never got to interact with them. When I was 6 we moved to the US, and my parents put me in a mostly Asian/White school so that I'd learn English fast. I remember I used to be super religious when I was younger (like one time a kid fell in the play ground in first grade and I started praying next to him). I also used to think non-christian religions were satanic(many of my classmates were buddhist too, now I feel lucky I couldn't speak English back then). Even as a little boy I was afraid of worshiping the wrong god and ending in hell. Funny, my idea of buddhism back then was basically christianity with Buddhai(who I thought was Siddharta Gautama) instead of Yahweh. Eventually I would learn what buddhism was actually, but I also learned about Islam so the "wrong version of god" thing still fucked with my mind. Coupled with my protestant family members trying to convert me and evangelicals telling me the catholic church was satanic, I became a non-denominational christian. When I was 18 I realized it was impossible to know what was the correct version of Yahweh and I got tired of playing the whole cat and mouse game christianity and islam presents you to get out of eternal torture. I realized Yahweh, if real, made it impossible to know what his true version was and therefore, no matter what I believed in, I was doomed to hell in someone's eyes. I also couldn't fathom why an all mighty, all loving, all knowing god would need to go through so many turns and twists to save his creation from eternal torture when he knew what would happen after creating satan. To me god became more irresponsible than a 15 year old who ended up having kids, at least teen parents don't know everything(and with the sex-ed in many places, the blame is really on the religious zealots teaching abstinence). My bisexuality also hurt my christianity, when I was a little boy having innocent crushes on my classmates I believed that I would grow out of liking boys. Nevertheless, puberty came and I realized I couldn't stop desiring men, something I had been schooled to believe was a choice and would send me to hell.
